 Order

The present miscellaneous appeals under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 have been filed by the respective appellants/claimants taking exception to the impugned order dated 04.10.2021 passed by learned Member, IX Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni (MP) in MACC No.247 of 2015 and MACC No.167 of 2015 seeking enhancement of amount of compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal.

entities.text: IX Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Vide order dated 04.10.2021 passed by the learned Claims Tribunal, three claim petitions have been decided, which were filed on behalf of one deceased and two injured persons arising out of the same accident.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58108 2 MA-3519-2022 2.
Since both these appeals have arisen out of the common award, therefore, they are heard together and are being disposed of by this common order.
However, for the sake of brevity, the facts are taken from MA No.3519 of 2022.
The parties shall be referred to by their rank in the learned Tribunal.

sentences.text: The facts of the case reveal that the date of accident is 11.02.2015.
At around 11:10 A.M., the claimants were going on a motorcycle from Katni to Kemor.
At the same time, offending truck bearing No.CG15A6818 being driven in rash and negligent manner by respondent No.1 met with an accident with the vehicle of the claimants.

Due to said accident, Raja Singh, aged 16 years (son of appellants/claimants in MA No.69 of 2022), who was riding the two-wheeler died in the said accident and Pavan Kumar Mishra (appellant in MA No.3519 of 2022) and another injured - Sonu Kumar Singh @ Prashant Kumar Singh sustained injures on various parts of their body.

entities.text: Sonu Kumar Singh @ Prashant Kumar Singh
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: Three different claim petitions were preferred.

Injured Pawan Kumar Mishra filed Claim Case No.247 of 2015, Injured Sonu Kumar Singh @ Prashant Kumar Singh filed Claim Case No.283 of 2015 and Claim Case No.167 of 2015 was preferred by Pappu @ Shobha Singh, legal representative of deceased Raja Singh.

entities.text: Sonu Kumar Singh @ Prashant Kumar Singh
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: All these claim petitions were heard together and decided vide a common order dated 04.10.2021 and the same is under scanner in the present misc. appeals.
4. The learned Claims Tribunal vide impugned order dated 04.10.2021 has partly allowed the claim petitions.

While allowing the claim petitions the learned Tribunal was of the view that the accidental two-wheeler was being ridden by deceased Raja Singh, who was minor at the time of accident and therefore the case falls under the category of contributory negligence and the claimants are liable to get 50% of the claim amounts.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58108 3 MA-3519-2022 5.
Two claimants have approached this Court for enhancement of the awarded amounts.
To render the impugned award, learned Tribunal has relied upon evidence of injured persons, who are eyewitness to the incident and other evidence available on record.
As per permanent Disability Certificate (Ex. P 438 & 439), Injured- Pawan had suffered disability of 50% due to injuries suffered on head and spinal cord.
The learned Tribunal has not granted any compensation on account of "disability" suffered by injured Pawan Singh.
On the strength of evidence recorded, impugned award has been rendered.

The break-up of compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal to injured-Pawan is as under:-

1. Compensation towards loss of earning 6,05,778/-
2. Compensation towards treatment & medical bills 18,75,454/-
3. Loss of future prospects 2,42,311/-
4. Expenses relating to transportation, nourishing food 1,00,000/-
5. Expenses for keeping an assistant 6,48,000/-
TOTAL 34,71,543/-

On the contrary, learned counsel for appellant-Injured refutes the aforesaid stand taken on behalf of Insurer and submits that the quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal is inadequate.

Enhancement of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:58108 4 MA-3519-2022 compensation is sought in the case of Injured-Pavan by submitting that "functional disability" of Injured- Pavan deserves to be taken at 100%, as he has lost his livelihood due to the injuries sustained in this accident and he has no future.
It is also submitted that the Tribunal has erred in assessing "future prospects" on lower side while assessing the loss of earning capacity in the case of Injured- Pavan.

7. On behalf of Injured- Pavan it is submitted by learned counsel that no compensation amount has been granted on account of permanent disability suffered by Injured- Pavan which is inadequate and it deserves to be enhanced.
It is pointed out that as per Certificates (Ex. P - 438 & 439), the "future medical expenses" are much more and the Tribunal has erred in not granting compensation under this head.

8. So far as compensation granted to injured-Pawan is concerned, it is submitted by counsel for the Insurer that the impugned award is challenged on the ground of contributory negligence and also that the awarded compensation is exorbitant and it ought to be on lower side looking to the factor of contributory negligence.
It is next submitted that compensation granted under various heads is without any basis, as no doctor has deposed regarding the future course of treatment for injured- Pavan.
Hence, it is submitted that the compensation awarded to Pawan has to be suitably reduced.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company (henceforth referred to as the "Insurer") contends that motorcycle rider - Raja Singh was a minor and he could not legally ride the motorcycle.
It is further submitted that there were two pillion riders on the motorcycle in question, which is prohibited in law.

Counsel for Insurer further submits that compensation so granted by the learned Tribunal is on higher side and without considering the medical evidence NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:58108 5 MA-3519-2022
the impugned award has been passed.
It is also submitted that the interest at the rate of 6% per annum payable on the awarded compensation is exorbitant.

Lastly, he submitted that looking to the facts of the present case, compensation granted by the learned Tribunal deserves to be brought in tune with the Constitution Bench decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of impugned award,
evidence on record and the decision cited, I find that motorcycle rider - Raja Singh was a minor and was not legally competent to ride a motorcycle.

Whether there were two pillion riders or one, is not of significance, as the aspect of motorcycle rider being a minor or of there being two pillion riders on the motorcycle, cannot by itself justify the finding of contributory negligence.

The manner in which this accident took place,
can be gathered from the evidence of Injured persons who are eyewitnesses also.
As per evidence of the injured persons they were going on the road and the driver of the offending vehicle had overtaken them and has dashed their motorcycle.
It is of common knowledge that when a vehicle tries to overtake another vehicle then the speed of the vehicle has to be exceeded.
Thus, the negligence on the part of driver is seen.

On scrutiny of aforesaid evidence, I find that negligence was of driver of the insured vehicle and there is no justification to conclude that the accident in question had taken place due to contributory negligence of the injured.

Such a view is being taken in view of a recent Supreme Court decision in the case of Sri Dinesh Kumar J.
@ Dinesh J Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.

With regard to the apportionment of contributory negligence at 50%-
50% on the part of the claimants and on the driver of the offending tractor as determined by the Claims Tribunal, I refer to the judgment of this Court in Juju NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

sentences.text: Reported in AIR 2013 SC 2293 as it is applicable to facts of the case on hand.
In the above case, Joy Kuruvila (the deceased) had a head-on collision with a bus approaching from the opposite side.
Joy Kuruvila sustained serious injuries and died on the way to the hospital.
The Tribunal found that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus driver.
It apportioned the contributory negligence between the driver and the deceased in the ratio of 75:25%.

On the basis of the pleadings and evidence on record, in the above said case, this Court has held thus on the negligence of the driver of the bus:-

4 "20.5.

sentences.text:
The mere position of the vehicles after accident, as shown in a scene mahazar,
cannot give a substantial proof as to the rash and negligent driving on the part of one or the other.

When two vehicles coming from opposite directions collide, the position of the vehicles and its direction, etc. depends on a number of factors like the speed of vehicles, intensity of collision, reason for collision, place at which one vehicle hit the other, etc.

From the scene of the accident, one may suggest or presume the manner in which the accident was caused, but in the absence of any direct or corroborative evidence, no conclusion can be drawn as to whether there was negligence on the part of the driver.
In absence of such direct or corroborative evidence, the Court cannot give any specific finding about negligence on the part of any individual."

12. Therefore, having regard to the totality of the case on hand and after re- appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence available on file, this court finds answer to the issue No.1 in favour of claimants and holds that the driver of offending vehicle was more negligent and contributed more to the occurrence of accident and re-fix the contributory negligence in the ratio of 70:30, i.e. 70% on the part of the driver of the tractor bearing Registration No.CG-15A6818 and 30% on the part of the rider of motorcycle, to safeguard the interest of both parties and to meet the ends of justice, as against the contributory negligence fixed by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58108 7 MA-3519-2022 Tribunal in the ratio of 50:50, on the part of the rider of motorcycle and on the part of the driver of tractor.
13. As per the contributory negligence re-fixed by this Court as above, in the ratio of 70:30, both the claimants are entitled to only 70% of the total compensation.

Accordingly, in case of Pavan Singh,
70% of Rs.34,71,543/- works out to Rs.24,30,080/- as against Rs.17,35,711/- awarded by learned Tribunal, after deducting 50%.
There would be enhancement of compensation by a sum of Rs.6,94,369/-.
In case of Raja Singh, 70% of Rs.9,77,200/- works out to Rs.6,84,040/- as against Rs.4,88,600/- awarded by learned Tribunal, after deducting 50%.
There would be enhancement of compensation by a sum of Rs.1,95,440/-.
14. So far as the quantum of compensation in all the heads are concerned, the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and no interference is called for.
15. In the light of the facts and circumstances of the case, as stated above, the appeals filed by the claimants are allowed in part.
The impugned common judgment and award dated 04th October 2021, passed in MACC 167 of 2015 and MACC No. 247 of 2015 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni, are hereby modified.

The contributory negligence fixed on the rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the tractor bearing Registration No.CG 15 A 6818 in the ratio of 50:50 is hereby set aside and the same is hereby modified, by re-fixing contributory negligence in the ratio of 70:30, i.e. 70% on the part of the driver of the tractor, bearing Registration No.CG 15 A 6818, and 30% on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, to meet the ends of justice.

16. As per the contributory negligence fixed at 70% on the part of the driver of tractor bearing Registration No.CG-15A 6818, the claimants are entitled NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:58108 8 MA-3519-2022 to only 70% of the total compensation.
